newsitem.title: CUBA: BOXING-CUBAN HEAVYWEIGHT SAVON SUFFERS UPSET DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CUBAN HEAVYWEIGHT SAVON SUFFERS UPSET DEFEAT.

text.p: Cuba's Felix Savon, five times world amateur heavyweight champion and twice Olympic champion, was sensationally knocked out by compatriot Juan Cause Delis in the quarter-finals of the national championships.

With 24 seconds remaining in the fourth round, Savon, easily ahead on points, took a fearsome right hook square on the jaw and slumped face down on the canvas in one of the biggest upsets in amateur boxing.
Savon, 29, was unconscious for three minutes in the ring while Delis jumped around to wild applause from the crowd of 3,000 in Friday night's bout.
Savon, who has lost just four times in the last 11 years, was attended by a Cuban team doctor at the ringside but did not require hospital treatment.
"We are keeping an eye on him but he slept well and is recovering normally," team doctor Raul Fuyaca told reporters on Saturday. "He doesn't remember the punch, but that is normal," he added.
Delis, now the only man in the world to have beaten Savon twice -- the first time was in 1986 -- said on Saturday he had prepared hard for the fight.
"Felix and I are good friends out of the ring and we train together. It is a friendly rivalry," he said.
Savon, 29, was sanguine about his defeat. "It is normal for sportsmen to win and lose. The real test is how quickly you can pick yourself up," he said on Saturday.
